guides.favoredWhen: She waits for a wasted E and dives. Hold E, vary volleys, turtle harder.

keyTips.text: You push and sit under tower: the lane comes to her.
She dodges spells: sidesteps are her whole defense, so lead targets.
A wasted E is a free kill for her: never throw E first.

tips.text: She farms under tower: your push sets up her all-in, so slow-push.
She pokes between volleys: never double-volley predictably.
Your R charges increase per rank: vary the beam count.
E-down dives: no stun means no answer, so hold E.
Landed plus zoned: the Akali who never gets E never dives.

sources.author: Anguish333
sources.rankClaim: Master (profile badge; title claims 2000LP GrandMaster EUW and Challenger EUNE) · Akali main

guides.favoredWhen: She dodges and baits every spell and sets up ganks after 6. Hit skillshots, hold E, track her jungler.

keyTips.text: She tracks your cooldowns and punishes each one: Q, W and E all open a window (about {cd:101:Q}).
Her W speed bursts dodge your skillshots: lead the target.
She fakes autos to bait your spells: never throw the first spell.

tips.text: She forces the choice: poke her or push; push first, poke second.
She baits first: hold spells until she walks in.
After 6 she calls her jungler: ward and hold E for ganks.
You stand behind minions to block Charm: keep the wave between you.
Deny her free engages all game: angles never stop mattering.

sources.author: Hofibauer
sources.rankClaim: Rank 1 EUW/EUNE Xerath (title, no badge) · Xerath main

guides.favoredWhen: Another skillshot check. Keep range, punish her cooldowns, and respect her burst.

keyTips.text: You outrange her: keep the range, win the poke war.
She rushes tier-2 boots: movement answers your Q, so vary it.
She takes Second Wind: your poke war needs mana to outlast sustain.

tips.text: Her dodge-first laning beats predictable Qs: hold until she commits.
She waits for spent spells: never double-cast into her window.
Your cooldowns are much longer: every wasted spell is her window.
She walks at you when you waste spells: keep max range, never concede position.
Range plus mana: the range advantage is won on windows, not poke.

sources.author: Trisend3
sources.rankClaim: Challenger (title and profile badge) · Syndra main

guides.favoredWhen: Every gap-close is a kill and he brings junglers. Hold E, poke from max range, end it before Voltaic.

keyTips.text: Any gap-close is a kill: with no disengage you cannot shake his R.
He stands off-wave: Q both him and the wave.
Your E is your whole defense: a wasted E is his all-in signal.

early-lane.text: Zed often places Living Shadow before Death Mark so he can swap away from skillshots. Hold your crowd control until he has used the swap.

win-condition.text: Death Mark always lands Zed behind his target. Pre-aim crowd control and escapes behind you, not toward where he cast it.

tips.text: He skips First Strike: your range denies his proc.
He buys early boots: every sidestepped Q is HP you never get.
Death Mark always lands Zed behind his target. Pre-aim crowd control and escapes behind you, not toward where he cast it.
After Voltaic he farms you: the spike ends your poke phase.
Spellshield plus his R closes every fight: end it before his second item.

keyTips.text: Prioritize last hits over poke: take poke only when it costs no farm, and recover mana with passive autos, preferring safe champion hits for the larger return.
Recall toward a twelve-hundred gold first buy for Lost Chapter; when forced back earlier, take Dark Seal to begin collecting stacks.

In team fights, stay behind the frontline and poke low-health carries before using the ultimate to start or finish the fight, reaching the longer level-sixteen sequence to pressure isolated carries into defensive summoners or kills.

tips.text: Open Doran's Ring with two Health Potions as the standard setup.
At level six, look for nearby kills and objective fights with Rite of the Arcane while tracking the opposing mid laner.
Protect the mid tower with safe waveclear; the first mid tower gives important map control.
When another lane takes mid and Xerath moves to a side lane, clear waves on his own side of the map and rotate back toward mid.
Never roam alone through river while the enemy mid and jungler are missing; Xerath alone there is an easy catch.
Contribute to skirmishes from a safer position with the long-range ultimate, then return to lane without giving up unnecessary farm.
Remember that E is the hard stun and its duration grows with the orb's travel distance; lead with longer-range casts for the longer lock.
Stay off extended side lanes: Xerath is immobile and weak alone, so never push where opponents can collapse on him.
Chip the frontline rather than forcing a risky dive when no carry angle is available, keeping the poke threat alive for the next ultimate window.

itemization.text: Run Arcane Comet with Manaflow Band, Transcendence, and Scorch plus Cut Down and Presence of Mind, pairing Comet with the lane-poke plan and Presence of Mind with mana sustain.

Build Luden's Echo first for damage and waveclear, then Horizon Focus for cooldowns and reliable ultimate access, preferring Horizon Focus over Shadowflame in the standard route while keeping Shadowflame as the snowball purchase when ahead.

Into tank-heavy teams take the Blackfire Torch, Sorcerer's Shoes, Liandry's Torment, Void Staff, Rabadon's Deathcap alternative, with Shadowflame, Rabadon's Deathcap, Void Staff, and Sorcerer's Shoes as standard endgame options and Zhonya's Hourglass for survival.

sources.author: Hofibauer
sources.rankClaim: Rank 1 EUW/EUNE Xerath (title, no badge) · Xerath main

keyTips.text: Harass with Arcanopulse and Eye of Destruction; the Eye of Destruction slow makes it easier to land Arcanopulse and Shocking Orb.
Save Shocking Orb as self-peel rather than spending it carelessly; a missed stun can leave Xerath open to an all-in.
When Rite of the Arcane is ready, poke first and then use it to finish a low target from range; cast from a position that cannot be interrupted immediately.

tips.text: Xerath is immobile and his charged Arcanopulse can be interrupted, so do not channel where enemy crowd control can reach him.
After bot tower falls, rotate mid, pressure the tower, and use poke to keep the defender away from objectives.
Against a healthy enemy pair, hold Shocking Orb for an approaching diver instead of throwing it into the wave.
Delay a full fight while Arcanopulse poke lowers targets, then join when the enemy is sufficiently softened.
Track the next major objective and establish vision safely before retreating to the team.
Support Xerath is vulnerable while warding or moving alone, so take a teammate on routes through uncertain areas.
Level six gives long-range Rite of the Arcane access; level nine maxes Arcanopulse and increases poke threat.
The next ultimate point at level eleven improves cleanup, and Eye of Destruction reaches max rank at level thirteen for a stronger Arcanopulse follow-up.
Ward major objectives and high-traffic routes late to reveal enemy movement.
Do not ward alone without knowing enemy positions; a pick on Xerath leaves the team in a four-versus-five.
Peel for allies with Shocking Orb and slow threats with Eye of Destruction instead of trying to stand in front.
Use range and fog to pressure squishies, but keep a safe position for the ultimate channel.

itemization.text: Take Arcane Comet, Manaflow Band, Transcendence, and Scorch with Coup de Grace and Presence of Mind as the 16.21 rune page.
Build the popular path of Zaz'Zak's Realmspike, Sorcerer's Shoes, Luden's Echo, Shadowflame, and Rabadon's Deathcap.
Start with Health Potion, Amplifying Tome, and Stealth Ward.
Choose Horizon Focus to replace Shadowflame in the fourth slot for longer-range damage or against immobilized targets.
Max Q, then W, then E, taking Rite of the Arcane at levels six, eleven, and sixteen.
